history.dynasty: Jadeja (founded at Nawanagar/Jamnagar under Jadeja patronage)
history.period: Founded 1630 (17th century); shrine built around two 400-year-old Khijda trees
history.summary: The Khijada Temple, formally Shri 5 Navtanpuri Dham, is the Acharyapith (principal seat) and origin place of the Shri Krishna Pranami Dharma (Nijanand Sampradaya), a Hindu tradition that also preaches the unity of all religions. It was founded in 1630 when Sadguru Shri Devchandraji (Nijanand Swami Shri Devchandreji) entered what was then a garden: he cleaned his teeth with a Khijda tree twig, broke it in two and planted the pieces, which grew into the two sacred trees still attached to the shrine walls. Devchandraji stayed here 25 years, and the second acharya Mahamati Shri Prannathji took shelter under him here and had his soul awakened. The temple stands near Khambhalia/Bedi Gate (Khijada Mandir Chowk), Jamnagar; it offers free food, lodging and parking to pilgrims.

name: Khijada Temple
town_description: Jamnagar is a coastal city in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, on the Gulf of Kutch, founded in 1540 by Jam Rawal of the Jadeja Rajput clan as Nawanagar. Nicknamed 'Chhoti Kashi' (Little Kashi) for its many temples, it is a major pilgrim and tourist hub whose landmarks include Lakhota Lake, the Lakhota Palace museum and the Bala Hanuman temple. The city is also an industrial centre, home to one of the world's largest oil refining complexes at nearby Motikhavdi.

travel.railway: Jamnagar railway station, about 2-3 km away (verify).
travel.road: Near Bedi Gate / Khambhalia Gate in the city centre; easily reached by auto-rickshaw or taxi.
